name: Determine high-performing and/or scalable network architectures

lesson.summary: Network performance comes from putting content close to users (CloudFront), using the AWS backbone for any protocol (Global Accelerator), choosing the right load balancer, steering users with Route 53, and using dedicated connectivity (Direct Connect) for hybrid workloads.
keyPoints: CloudFront caches content at edge locations
Global Accelerator listeners support TCP and UDP, and it routes traffic over the AWS global network
ALB works at layer 7 and routes on request content such as path; NLB works at layer 4, can handle millions of requests per second, and has a static IP address per enabled AZ
Route 53 latency routing sends users to the lowest-latency Region
Direct Connect is a dedicated private network connection to AWS; Site-to-Site VPN is the internet-based alternative

scenarios.text: A company must replicate about 10 Gbps of data continuously from its on-premises data center to AWS. Over its current internet VPN, throughput and latency vary widely and the nightly replication window is regularly missed.

questions.prompt: A website serves large static images from an S3 bucket in one Region to users worldwide, and users far from the Region see slow load times. What should the architect add?

options.text: An Amazon CloudFront distribution with the bucket as origin
A larger EC2 instance in front of S3
An additional NAT gateway
An S3 lifecycle rule to Glacier

questions.explanation: CloudFront caches content at edge locations close to users and lowers latency. A larger EC2 instance, a NAT gateway or a lifecycle rule does nothing for geographic distance.

questions.prompt: A multiplayer game uses UDP and needs static IP addresses and the lowest latency for players around the world, routing them to the nearest healthy endpoint. Which service fits?

options.text: Amazon CloudFront
AWS Global Accelerator
Application Load Balancer only
Amazon Route 53 simple routing

questions.explanation: Global Accelerator provides static anycast IP addresses, its listeners support TCP and UDP, and it routes traffic over the AWS global network to healthy endpoints. CloudFront is a content delivery network for caching content, an ALB works at layer 7 for application traffic and is not the fit for a UDP game, and simple routing returns records without latency steering or static IPs.

questions.prompt: Which TWO statements about Elastic Load Balancing are correct?

options.text: A Network Load Balancer works at layer 4 and can handle millions of requests per second
An Application Load Balancer supports path-based routing
A Classic Load Balancer is the recommended choice for new path-based routing designs
A Network Load Balancer routes traffic based on HTTP header contents
An Application Load Balancer provides one static IP address per AZ by default

questions.explanation: The NLB guide states it works at the fourth layer and can handle millions of requests per second, and the ALB guide lists path conditions for routing on the request URL. The ALB guide lists path routing as a benefit over the Classic Load Balancer, so a Classic Load Balancer is not the choice for new path-based designs. An NLB works at layer 4, not on HTTP headers, and static IP addresses per enabled AZ are described in the NLB guide, not as an ALB default.

questions.statement: Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing can direct users to the AWS Region that gives them the lowest network latency.
questions.explanation: True. Latency routing returns the record for the Region with the lowest measured latency to the user.

questions.prompt: Which connectivity option best meets the steady, high-bandwidth, low-jitter requirement?

options.text: Site-to-Site VPN over the internet
AWS Direct Connect
A NAT gateway
VPC peering

questions.explanation: Direct Connect provides a dedicated private connection with consistent bandwidth and latency. VPN traffic crosses the public internet and varies, a NAT gateway only provides outbound internet access from private subnets, and VPC peering connects VPCs, not data centers.

questions.prompt: Direct Connect provisioning will take several weeks, but the company needs encrypted connectivity to AWS right away. What should the architect do in the meantime?

options.text: Wait for Direct Connect before moving any data
Open the databases to the internet
Use VPC peering to the on-premises network
Set up an AWS Site-to-Site VPN as interim connectivity

questions.explanation: Site-to-Site VPN can be created quickly and encrypts traffic with IPsec, so it works as an interim or backup path. Waiting delays the project, exposing databases publicly is insecure, and VPC peering cannot reach an on-premises network.
